title: The sell sheet checks a start date more loosely than the payment sheet checks a payment date
what: Two different date rules live side by side. Taking a payment refuses a date that is not a real day or has a mistyped year (the payment sheet notes a year 0002 once reached storage). Selling a plan only checks that the start date has the right shape: an owner who mistypes the year (2016 or 0002) gets no error and no question, because the unusual-date question only asks about starts far AHEAD. The plan is saved long ended.
expected: One date rule for every money form: a real calendar day, not before the earliest sensible date, and a question for a start far in the past as well as far ahead.
fix_line: Use the same real-date and earliest-date check for the plan start as for the payment date, and ask once about a start far in the past

title: Some tests of the desk forms only look for words in the code, not at what the form does
what: Three tests that name the sell, collect and add-member forms read the form file as text and check that a line of code or a sentence is in it. They pass even if that line is never reached or the form shows something else, and fail on a harmless rename.
expected: These checks open the form (or call the logic it uses) and check what the person sees or what gets saved.
fix_line: Replace the text-search checks with checks of what the form shows or saves
